Article Title: Oil tumbles over 6% as Trump's Iran talks revive hopes of easing Middle East tensions
Article Text: Oil prices tumbled more than 6% on Monday as hopes of a diplomatic breakthrough between the United States and Iran erased part of last month's rally. However, uncertainty over the negotiations and persistent security risks along key shipping routes has kept investors on edge.As of 7:10 am, WTI crude was down 4.75% at $80.65 a barrel, while Brent crude fell 4.40% to $84.06 a barrel.Earlier, Brent crude futures dropped more than 6% to $82.41 after US President Donald Trump said talks with Iran would be held on Monday. The announcement followed his decision to call off an imminent attack on Iran in a bid to reach an agreement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and resolve the deadlock over Tehran's nuclear capabilities.The sharp decline followed a rally of more than 20% in both benchmark contracts last month, fuelled by renewed conflict between the US and Iran and attacks on several tankers near Oman. The incidents heightened security concerns and discouraged shippers from entering the Gulf to load oil.Trump also signalled a possible easing of tensions over the weekend. Writing on his Truth Social platform late on Saturday, he said Iran and other Middle Eastern countries had asked for time to finalise a deal that would ensure "the Immediate, Complete and Total" reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and "an end to Iran's nuclear threat".While hopes of an agreement lifted sentiment, questions remained over whether the diplomatic effort would succeed."The bigger focus is whether this week turns into a rinse and repeat of last week — with hopes of a deal collapsing as Iran digs in its heels and continues to leverage its control over the Strait, potentially through an attack on a US base or a tanker transiting the waterway," IG market analyst Tony Sycamore told Reuters.Meanwhile, developments in regional shipping painted a mixed picture.Shipping data showed two Saudi oil tankers crossed the Bab el-Mandeb Strait from the Red Sea over the weekend, while movement through the Strait of Hormuz slowed following reports of vessel attacks.The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations said three more tanker attacks had been reported since Saturday.Separately, OPEC+ agreed on Sunday to raise its oil production quota by around 188,000 barrels a day from September, completing the unwinding of one layer of voluntary output cuts.Even with the planned increase, the market has seen little impact. Export disruptions in the Gulf, Russia and Kazakhstan caused by the Iran and Ukraine wars have meant most of OPEC+'s monthly output hikes this year have not translated into additional supply.
Article Summary: WTI crude was down 4.75% at $80.65 a barrel, while Brent crude fell 4.40% to $84.06 a barrel. The sharp decline followed a rally of more than 20% in both benchmark contracts last month, fuelled by renewed conflict between the US and Iran.

Article Title: India's deep-sea bet: Centre's 'Samudra Manthan' to churn crude — How it works
Article Text:
How the scheme will work



What are experts saying



A long-term exploration push



Months of turmoil in the Middle East have wrecked global energy supplies, forcing countries to rethink their energy security strategies. India, however, is looking inward.Rather than relying more heavily on imports, the government is betting on finding more oil and gas beneath its own seas by sharing the financial risks of deepwater exploration, an area companies have long avoided because of the high costs and uncertain returns.Last week, the Union Cabinet approved the Rs 84,084 crore Samudra Manthan National Offshore Exploration Scheme, under which the Centre will fund 50% of the cost of drilling a deepwater or ultra-deepwater exploration well, or up to Rs 650 crore per well, whichever is lower. Officials said the support will cover 60 exploration wells over the next five years."This perhaps is the first time that any government in the world is funding risk exploration from the budget," an official said.The programme comes as India continues to depend heavily on imported energy. Officials said crude oil imports have risen from 77% to 88% of the country's requirement over the past decade. India also imports around half of the natural gas it consumes, which is used for fertiliser production, power generation, CNG and piped cooking gas.According to officials cited by PTI, the recent conflict in the Middle East, which disrupted energy supplies, highlighted the need to strengthen domestic production and reduce reliance on overseas supplies.Officials said companies have largely focused on producing oil and gas from known discoveries while investing little in searching for new reserves, as unsuccessful exploration wells result in complete financial losses."They were spending money only on development drilling -- producing already established discoveries. Hardly any money went into risk exploration, which is key to finding new resources," an official said.To encourage companies to drill in deepwater and ultra-deepwater areas, the government will absorb part of the exploration cost."Samudra Manthan is, in that sense, a game-changing scheme," another official added.The benefit will be available to companies holding blocks awarded under previous Open Acreage Licensing Programme (OALP) rounds as well as those securing acreage in the ongoing bidding round. Eligible companies can claim government support of up to Rs 650 crore for each qualifying exploration well.Officials said the scheme has also been designed to attract global energy companies to India's offshore basins.The biggest share of the Rs 84,084 crore outlay has been earmarked for exploration itself.Of the total allocation, Rs 43,200 crore has been set aside over five years till 2031 for deepwater and ultra-deepwater drilling, translating to roughly Rs 650 crore each for the 60 planned exploration wells.Another Rs 28,534 crore will be spent on offshore seismic and geological surveys to identify prospective drilling locations.The scheme also earmarks Rs 10,000 crore for common infrastructure, including subsea pipelines and onshore oil and gas receipt and processing facilities, while Rs 2,000 crore has been allocated to develop oil and gas manufacturing and services zones.Apart from funding exploration, the government plans to create infrastructure that can be shared by multiple operators.Through its Common Hub Infrastructure (CHI) component, the scheme aims to develop shared pipelines and processing facilities so discoveries made by different companies can be commercialised using common assets instead of building separate infrastructure for every project.Officials said this could lower development costs, improve project economics, optimise marine engineering and offshore resources, make hydrocarbon evacuation more efficient, simplify offshore logistics, speed up commercialisation of smaller discoveries and improve the viability of deepwater and ultra-deepwater projects.Prashant Vashisht, senior vice president, ICRA Ltd, said the scheme addresses two major challenges in offshore exploration. "The scheme provides funds for offshore seismic data acquisition especially in erstwhile No-Go zones, which is a key issue hampering commercial exploitation of oil and gas reserves in these areas due to lack of good prospectivity data."Additionally, the scheme provides support for drilling deepwater/ultra-deepwater wells where the domestic Upstream sector has limited experience and technical expertise and exploitation of the same remains highly capital intensive and risky. The scheme aims to add incremental annual production of 10-15 million tonne of oil equivalent which would reduce the dependence on imports of oil and gas but only to the extent of 3-5%," he told PTI.Officials expect the scheme to increase exploration across India's offshore basins, attract investment from international energy companies and help unlock hydrocarbon reserves that remain unexplored.They said the initiative is intended as a long-term effort, noting that deepwater exploration is inherently uncertain and not every well drilled under the programme will lead to a commercial discovery.Officials also said the government's decision to directly fund exploration risk marks a departure from its earlier approach of supporting only proven development.The scheme builds on a series of policy reforms introduced since 1997. India shifted from production-sharing contracts to the Hydrocarbon Exploration and Licensing Policy (HELP) in 2016, introducing Revenue Sharing Contracts, the Open Acreage Licensing Policy (OALP), a uniform licence, and marketing and pricing freedom.The government later adopted a hybrid allocation model for under-commercialised basins, giving greater weight to work commitments in unexplored areas. These reforms were consolidated under the Oilfields (Regulation and Development) Amendment Act, 2025, which came into effect in April and laid the foundation for the 50 exploration blocks offered under OALP, small-field and coal-bed methane bidding rounds in December 2025.
Article Summary: The Centre will fund 50% of the cost of drilling a deepwater or ultra-deepwater exploration well, or up to Rs 650 crore per well, whichever is lower. Officials said the support will cover 60 exploration wells over the next five years. The programme comes as India continues to depend heavily on imported energy.

Article Title: New stock market timings from August 3: What has changed?
Article Text: Final minutes of the trading day are set to change from Monday, August 3, as the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) is introducing a new Closing Auction Session for F&O-eligible stocks and extending trading hours for the equity derivatives segment.The new framework brings a different end-of-day routine for traders, especially those in F&O-eligible stocks and the equity derivatives segment. Here's a look at what will change starting this week.Under the revised trading framework, biggest change will be seen in the closing process for F&O-eligible (Category I) stocks. Instead of ending with the regular trading session alone, these stocks will now move into a dedicated auction process after 3:15pm, with the auction-discovered price becoming their official closing price.Regular trading for F&O-eligible stocks will end at 3:15pm, followed by a five-minute transition period until 3:20pm. The Closing Auction Session will then begin with CAS Order Entry I from 3:20pm to 3:25pm and CAS Order Entry II from 3:25pm to 3:30pm.During the second order entry window, market orders cannot be modified or cancelled. At the same time, the session will also close randomly within its final two minutes.Order matching will be carried out between 3:30pm and 3:35pm, after which the closing auction price will be determined. This price will be treated as the official closing price for all F&O-eligible stocks.The changes do not affect all stocks. Non-F&O equity cash stocks will continue to trade until 3:30pm, with no change in their existing market hours.Sebi has also extended trading in the equity derivatives (F&O) segment by 10 minutes. From August 3, trading in this segment will continue until 3:40pm, while operating hours for other market segments will remain unchanged.The regulator has also revised the pre-opening session.Under the new schedule, order entry will take place from 9:00 am to 9:07 am, followed by order matching between 9:07am and 9:15am. The regular trading session will continue to start at 9:15 am.According to Sebi, the Closing Auction Session is intended to ensure a fair and transparent closing price through an auction mechanism. It said the framework is designed to improve execution efficiency by aggregating liquidity, provide equal access to all investors, reduce tracking errors for passive funds, and align India's market structure with global best practices.
Article Summary: Sebi is introducing a new Closing Auction Session for F&O-eligible stocks and extending trading hours for the equity derivatives segment. The changes do not affect all stocks. Non-F&O equity cash stocks will continue to trade until 3:30pm, with no change in their existing market hours.

Article Title: Rupee rises 31 paise on weaker dollar, lower oil prices and continued FII inflows
Article Text: Falling gobal crude oil prices and weaker US dollar lifted rupee higher in early trade on Monday. The currency traded at a gain of 31 paise against US dollar, while drawing support from foreign fund inflows, higher forex reserves and continued intervention by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), according to forex traders.Rupee opened at 95.15 against the US dollar in the interbank foreign exchange market before strengthening further to 95.12, marking a gain of 31 paise over its previous close of 95.43. The rise comes after the currency ended Friday 7 paise stronger, extending its positive run for a fifth consecutive session.The improvement in sentiment followed developments in the Middle East after US President Donald Trump said he had decided against carrying out planned strikes on Iran.On Sunday, Trump said American forces had been prepared to launch what he described as "the biggest attack since World War II". However, he said he chose to put the plan on hold after requests from Gulf allies Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates, as well as appeals from unnamed Iranian officials. He also said he had spoken with key Gulf leaders, including Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, before deciding to give diplomacy more time.The easing of geopolitical concerns was reflected in oil markets, with Brent crude falling 5% to $83.66 a barrel. The dollar index, which tracks the US currency against six major peers, was also lower by 0.17% at 99.74.Explaining the factors supporting the rupee, Anil Kumar Bhansali, head of treasury and executive director, Finrex Treasury Advisors LLP, said, "The rupee was supported by lower Brent crude oil prices, a weaker dollar, and sustained foreign portfolio inflows, and continued RBI presence in the foreign exchange market on Friday.""As Brent oil prices fell to $84 per barrel after Trump delayed strikes on Iran, the rupee opened at 95.15 on Monday and is expected to trade in the range of 95.00-95.50," he said.Apart from favourable global cues, domestic indicators also remained supportive. Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) purchased equities worth Rs 277.48 crore on a net basis on Friday, according to exchange data.The RBI's latest data, released on Friday, showed that India's foreign exchange reserves rose by $6.118 billion to $682.354 billion during the week ended July 24. In the previous reporting week, reserves had increased by $1.08 billion to $676.237 billion.Dalal Street also began the week on a firm footing. In early trade, Sensex climbed 470.06 points to 78,564.70, while Nifty gained 150 points to reach 24,532.95. Separately, data released by the Controller General of Accounts (CGA) showed that the Centre's fiscal deficit stood at 18.2% of the full-year target at the end of June.
Article Summary: Rupee opened at 95.15 against the US dollar in the interbank foreign exchange market before strengthening further to 95.12, marking a gain of 31 paise over its previous close of 95.43. The improvement in sentiment followed developments in the Middle East after US President Donald Trump said he had decided against carrying out planned strikes on Iran.

Article Title: Japan, US step in to support yen with rare joint intervention; Tokyo keeps door open for more action
Article Text: After joining hands in a rare currency market intervention, the US and Japan have left the door open for more coordinated action, with Tokyo saying it is ready to step in again if yen continues to swing.In a statement issued on Monday, Japan's ministry of finance said it intervened in the foreign exchange market on Friday, July 31, buying yen in coordination with the US department of the treasury. The move was aimed at addressing what it described as excessive volatility and disorderly movements in the Japanese currency.The ministry said the intervention was undertaken under the framework of the Japan-US Finance Ministers' Joint Statement issued in September 2025.It also announced plans to use the US Federal Reserve's Foreign and International Monetary Authorities (FIMA) Repo Facility in the future."Japan plans to utilize the Federal Reserve's "Foreign and International Monetary Authorities Repo Facility" (FIMA Repo Facility) in the future," it said.Emphasising that close coordination with Washington will continue, the Ministry said it remains in regular contact with the US Treasury and is prepared to intervene again if market conditions require it."The Ministry of Finance of Japan is closely monitoring the situation and maintaining tight communication with the US department of the treasury," it said, adding, "We will not hesitate to carry out further coordinated interventions in the future if necessary."Explaining the rationale behind the move, the ministry said the intervention was carried out under the September 2025 agreement between the two governments."This joint action was taken pursuant to the US-Japan Finance Ministers' Joint Statement issued in September 2025 and countered excessive volatility and disorderly movements in the Japanese yen in recent months," the Ministry noted.The currency action comes as Japan has also trimmed its economic growth outlook for the current fiscal year. According to Kyodo News, the government has cut its growth forecast to 0.9 per cent from 1.3 per cent, citing the impact of higher crude oil prices on the import-dependent economy.The government said a weaker yen against the US dollar, along with elevated crude oil prices due to the Middle East chaos, continues to pose risks to economic growth.
Article Summary: Japan's ministry of finance said it intervened in the foreign exchange market on Friday, July 31. The move was aimed at addressing what it described as excessive volatility and disorderly movements in the Japanese currency. The intervention was undertaken under the framework of the Japan-US Finance Ministers' Joint Statement issued in September 2025.

Article Title: Russian crude imports in July highest since Ukraine war
Article Text:
Russia’s share in India’s crude imports hits 55.5%

NEW DELHI: India’s crude oil imports from Russia climbed to a record 2.8 million barrels per day (mbd) in July accounting for more than half of the country’s purchases, even as refiners stepped up sourcing from West Asian suppliers with oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz normalised, reports Atul Mathur.India’s LPG imports remained heavily skewed towards US, which supplied over 9 lakh tonne, or about 73%, of the over 1.2 million tonne imported in July.July purchases were the highest since India began importing large volumes of discounted Russian crude following the outbreak of the Ukraine war in 2022.According to ship-tracking data from Kpler, India imported a little over 5 mbd of crude in July, marginally higher than in June.Supplies from Russia rose to 2.8 mbd from 2.7 mbd in June, taking its share in India’s crude imports to 55.5%.Nikhil Dubey, lead analyst at Kpler, said that amid the evolving geopolitical situation — earlier around the Strait of Hormuz and now around the Bab el-Mandeb Strait — Russian crude supplies have once again proven to be among the most reliable.“Another reason for the strong Russian imports is the continued availability of Russian cargo, as drone strikes on Russia’s refining infrastructure have reduced domestic refining activity, leaving more crude available for export,” Dubey said.While purchases from Russia have increased, refiners said discounts on Russian Urals crude have almost disappeared.The July data also suggest Indian refiners have started restoring purchases from West Asian suppliers after supply disruptions in the Persian Gulf during the conflict.Saudi Arabia recorded the biggest increase among major suppliers, with exports to India rising to 4.2 lakh barrels per day (bd) in July from 2.9 lakh bd in June. Imports from Iraq continued to recover after falling to zero in April, with purchases in July nearly doubling to 1.3 lakh bd from 67,100 bd in June, marking the third consecutive monthly increase since supplies resumed in May. Kuwait also returned to India’s import basket, shipping 51,600 bd after recording no exports during April, May and June.The return of Iraqi and Kuwaiti crude, along with higher imports from Saudi Arabia, suggests crude flows through the Strait of Hormuz have largely normalised after disruptions during the conflict, allowing Indian refiners to increase purchases from Gulf producers.Among other suppliers, imports from the UAE declined to 4.6 lakh bd in July from 5.1 lakh bd in June, though it remained India’s second-largest source of crude.
Article Summary: India’s crude oil imports from Russia climbed to a record 2.8 million barrels per day (mbd) in July. The purchases were the highest since India began importing large volumes of discounted Russian crude following the outbreak of the Ukraine war in 2022.

Article Title: RBI expected to hold rates on Aug 5
Article Text:
High frequency indicators, including industrial output and GST collections, point to resilient domestic activity.

MUMBAI: RBI is expected to leave interest rates unchanged at its monetary policy committee meeting on August 5 as economists see little case for an immediate policy move despite rising inflation risks, with rupee being stable, resilient domestic growth and uncertainty over crude oil prices shaping expectations.High frequency indicators, including industrial output and GST collections, point to resilient domestic activity. The main uncertainty lies abroad. Volatility in West Asia and its effect on crude oil prices remain the chief risk, while concerns over El Nino have receded, reducing the urgency for further monetary easing.According to Soumya Kanti Ghosh, chief economist, SBI group, “With CPI inflation likely to remain above 5% for the next two quarters and likely average of 5% in FY27, we believe RBI will maintain status quo”. He said that while the MPC may keep rates unchanged, the current backdrop has made soft language costlier. Oil volatility, rupee pressure, caution over external flows, and higher inflation projections make an explicitly dovish message less likely.Ghosh expects Q1 FY27 real GDP growth to outperform RBI’s earlier projection of 6.6% and come in at around 7.0%. He expects CPI inflation for Q1 at 3.9%, followed by 5.2% in Q2, 5.6% in Q3, and 5.0% in Q4, taking the FY27 average to around 5%.According to Ghosh, “A rate hold can still move markets if the statement shifts the balance between growth comfort and inflation / FX vigilance”.He said investors should watch RBI’s intervention in the short end of the forward book, where the short end forward position has reduced by $13 billion, alongside cumulative foreign inflows of around $35 billion through FCNR(B) deposits and other channels. He also pointed to the positive Indian Ocean Dipole, which stood at +0.44 degrees Celsius on July 26. The difference in sea surface temperatures between the western and eastern parts of the Indian Ocean could support rainfall and offset initial monsoon shortfalls.According to Santanu Sengupta and Arjun Varma of Goldman Sachs, the rupee is expected to stabilise following RBI measures to attract foreign capital. “With the INR having broadly stabilised following the RBI’s recent FX measures, we see limited need for the MPC to turn more hawkish near term”. They expect RBI to lower its inflation forecast modestly as crude oil prices remain below the $95 a barrel benchmark used at the June policy meeting.
Article Summary: RBI is expected to leave interest rates unchanged at its monetary policy committee meeting on August 5. High frequency indicators, including industrial output and GST collections, point to resilient domestic activity. The main uncertainty lies abroad. Volatility in West Asia and its effect on crude oil prices remain the chief risk.

Article Title: Househelp apps cross 1L orders as prices fall to Rs 29
Article Text: BENGALURU: On-demand house-help platforms Snabbit and Urban Company’s InstaHelp each crossed 1 lakh completed jobs on Sunday, as intense competition in the fast-growing category pushed the price of an hour’s household work to as little as Rs 29 in some locations.Snabbit said it had completed more than 1.15 lakh jobs by 6:50 pm on Sunday, with the tally expected to rise further by the end of the day.Urban Company said InstaHelp crossed one lakh delivered orders at 5:54 pm.The company described it as a peak-day milestone, adding that sustained volumes would depend on repeat usage, service quality and worker availability.The milestones came amid aggressive promotional pricing. App screenshots reviewed by TOI showed Urban Company offering 30 minutes of InstaHelp Standard for Rs 19, while 45-minute and one-hour bookings were priced at Rs 29 at the location checked—discounts of up to 88% from regular rates.Snabbit, too, was offering one-hour booking slots for Rs 29 in some locations, according to screenshots shared across social media.By around 7 pm on Sunday, however, Urban Company’s app showed instant service as unavailable at the location checked, with the earliest available slot being the following morning.InstaHelp promises to send a worker within 10-15 minutes for chores such as sweeping, mopping, dishwashing, laundry and basic meal preparation.Urban Company launched InstaHelp as a pilot in Mumbai in March last year and has since expanded the service to select neighbourhoods across major metros.“Crossing 100,000 delivered orders in a single day, barely five months after we crossed 50,000, reflects both the growing consumer demand for InstaHelp and the strength of the operating model we’ve built,” said Urban Company co-founder and CEO Abhiraj Singh Bhal.Snabbit has scaled from about 400 daily jobs to more than one lakh in under two years. It completed four million house-help jobs in the April-June quarter, including 1.51 million in June alone.The company said its cash burn per completed job fell by more than Rs 100 sequentially to below Rs 250.
Article Summary: Urban Company’s InstaHelp crossed one lakh delivered orders at 5:54 pm. Snabbit said it had completed more than 1.15 lakh jobs by 6:50 pm on Sunday. The milestones came amid aggressive promotional pricing. App screenshots reviewed by TOI showed Urban Company offering 30 minutes ofinstaHelp Standard for Rs 19.

Article Title: E-2-wheelers cross 2L mark as EV sales soar
Article Text: NEW DELHI/ CHENNAI: India’s EV market hit a new high in July with registrations across categories jumping over 66% to around 3.3 lakh units, compared with just under 2 lakh units in July 2025, amid elevated oil prices, a wider choice of models and expanding dealer networks. Last June 3.1 lakh EVs were registered across the country, according to Vahan data.Electric two-wheelers drove most of the growth, crossing 2-lakh monthly mark for first time. Registrations rose to 2,04,201 units in July from about 1.95 lakh in June and around 1.1 lakh in the year-ago period. Electric models accounted for around 11.2% of all two-wheelers registered in the month, up from 10.6% in June. Average monthly electric two-wheeler registrations have climbed to around 1.7 lakh units in 2026, compared with 1.1 lakh last year, reflecting stronger consumer acceptance and the growing availability of scooters across price segments.TVS Motor retained its leadership, registering 55,465 electric two-wheelers in July, up from 47,418 in June. Bajaj Auto remained second with 45,562 Chetak registrations, compared to 43,505 units in the previous month.Ather Energy ranked third, despite registrations easing to 30,317 units from 31,440 in June. Hero MotoCorp’s Vida increased volumes to 22,883 units from 21,893, while Ola Electric’s registrations declined to 14,102 units from 16,249.Electric passenger vehicles, however, lost some momentum after a record June. Registrations eased to 32,660 units from 33,441 in the preceding month, although sales remained significantly higher than a year earlier. Tata Motors maintained its lead in the electric car and SUV segment, with registrations rising to 13,568 units from 12,766 in June.
Article Summary: Electric two-wheelers drove most of the growth, crossing 2-lakh monthly mark for first time. TVS Motor retained its leadership, registering 55,465 electric two- wheelers in July. Electric passenger vehicles, however, lost some momentum after a record June.

Article Title: Investments in PE-VC fall 6% to $20.3bn in Jan-July
Article Text: CHENNAI: Private Equity-Venture Capital (PE-VC) in India crossed $20 billion mark in Jan-July this year (CY2026). However, it is nearly 6% lower than $21.5 billion recorded in the corresponding seven month period (Jan-July) last year (CY2025) .July 2026 recorded an investment of $3 billion, which is flat against $3.2 billion in the same month in 2025, data released by research firm Venture Intelligence showed. Global investment firm Brookfield’s Lumara, a renewable energy platform, led the PE-VC investments deals in July, with an investment of about $600 million. It took the cumulative investments to $20.3 billion this year comprising 756 deals. The PE-VC investments do not include those relating to the real estate sector.Arun Natarajan, founder, Venture Intelligence said, the investments highlighted the continued long-term faith global and domestic investors have in India’s private markets, amid geopolitical challenges and volatile public markets depressing IPO activity.“Healthy exits notched up by investors in recent months — including via the Meta-CRED deal and public market sales — offer a strong reason for optimism,” he told TOI.In recent months, PE investors are laying emphasis on sectors, such as infrastructure (especially renewable power companies), manufacturing (automobile and auto components in particular) and data centres, apart from the traditional sectors like NBFCs and healthcare.“VC investors are doubling down on B2B software startups, including special emphasis on AI-enabled companies like Sarvam AI and Emergent Labs,” he added.Natarajan said, private markets in India showed an impressive resilience across H1 2026. “So long as global macro conditions stay relatively stable, the total PE-VC deployment this year can be expected to land roughly on par with 2025,” he said.
Article Summary: Private Equity-Venture Capital (PE-VC) in India crossed $20 billion mark in Jan- July this year. However, it is nearly 6% lower than $21.5 billion recorded in the corresponding seven month period (Jan-July) last year (CY2025) July 2026 recorded an investment of $3 billion, which is flat against $3.2 billion in the same month in 2025.

Article Title: Education needs more capital, fewer curbs: Noel Tata
Article Text:
File photo: Noel Tata

BENGALURU: Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata on Sunday questioned restrictions on for-profit education, saying they discouraged investment in a sector where India needs far more quality colleges and universities.Speaking at IIMBue, an IIM Bangalore alumni meet in Bengaluru, Tata said only a small fraction of students secure admission to the country’s top institutions, forcing many high-performing students to pursue higher education overseas.“We spend an atrocious amount of money every year sending kids to the US and Europe,” he said.Tata said India should create enough world-class institutions so students do not have to leave the country for quality education and career opportunities.“I believe the courts have said that you can’t. An educational institution cannot be for profit, which is sad,” he said. “I think it’s preventing a lot of money from coming into education, into building the education system.”His remarks come as Tata Trusts partners with IIM Bangalore to establish its School of Undergraduate Studies. Tata said education would be a key focus area for the Trusts, which wants to return to building institutions as it did with the Indian Institute of Science, Tata Institute of Fundamental Research and Tata Memorial Hospital.“I’d like to start spending some more of our money on building new institutions,” he said.Healthcare is another priority. Tata said the Trusts plans to build 40-50 general hospitals across India.“We’re now looking to see if we can build 40 or 50 general-purpose hospitals across India,” he said. “We’ve identified three locations. We’re going to start that.”The hospitals will operate on a not -profit basis and aim to work within the funding available under govt health insurance schemes.The Trusts is also considering a cross-subsidy model under which 20-30% of rooms would be charged at commercial rates, helping subsidise treatment for the remaining patients.Tata said all patients would receive the same doctors, medicines and operating theatres. Those paying more would primarily get private rooms and additional facilities for their families.He also called for more rigorous ways to measure the impact of philanthropy, questioning broad claims that projects had “touched” thousands of lives without demonstrating what had actually changed. “We need to be clear about what we mean when we say ‘touch the lives of somebody’,” he said.
Article Summary: Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata questioned restrictions on for-profit education. Tata said India should create enough world-class institutions so students do not have to leave the country for quality education and career opportunities. He said the Trusts plans to build 40-50 general hospitals across India.

Article Title: West Asia war uncertainty keeps businesses on edge
Article Text: MUMBAI: A prolonged war in West Asia is making it difficult for companies to manage their costs—the persistent volatility be it in terms of commodity inflation, freight charges or exchange rates means nothing can be planned with certainty. While rising costs will squeeze margins, some of the businesses are also wary that discretionary demand may take a hit amid multiple rounds of price increases.“For companies like ours, the biggest uncertainties stem from volatility in commodity prices/raw material costs, freight costs and shipping timelines, all of which can impact supply chain planning. It forces us to double down on execution, enforce cost-discipline and diversify sourcing,” said Shrikant Kanhere, MD & CEO at AWL Agri Business.Pricing products is becoming a challenge because there is no stability in rates, said Mayank Shah, chief marketing officer at Parle Products.Continued uncertainty will push companies to postpone capital deployment weighing on fresh job additions and broader demand, said B. Thiagarajan, MD at Blue Star. “This whole FY will be strained. When costs go up, both margins and consumer demand get impacted,” Thiagarajan said.In their recent quarterly earnings, companies have said that commodity inflation continues to be a major headwind, projecting more price hikes going ahead.“A protracted conflict in West Asia, alongside emerging El Nino conditions that may weaken monsoons and intensify heatwaves, could weigh on growth, inflation and current account,” ITC said, highlighting trade and supply chain disruptions in Q1.Prolonged geopolitical conflicts may increase uncertainty for businesses in the short-term, said Ashok Nair, MD, RPG Life Sciences, adding that the firm’s continued expansion into new and emerging markets offers it some operational buffers. For consumers, supply chain volatility will translate into more price hikes across the board, potentially making festive shopping pricier. “.....if need be we will also make further pricing interventions because we’re also coming to terms with the exact inflationary impact on the margins,” said Ashish Goenka, group CFO at Tata Consumer Products in recent earnings call.Mohit Malhotra, global CEO at Dabur India said inflationary pressures are expected going forward.
Article Summary: A prolonged war in West Asia is making it difficult for companies to manage their costs. The persistent volatility in commodity inflation, freight charges or exchange rates means nothing can be planned with certainty. While rising costs will squeeze margins, businesses are also wary that discretionary demand may take a hit amid multiple rounds of price increases.

Article Title: China gets just 1 FDI approval in India in FY26, Hong Kong secures 13 proposals
Article Text:
Press Note 3 eased



China remains a small source of FDI



China's share in India's foreign direct investment (FDI) approvals remained largely negligible in 2025-26, with the government approving just one proposal worth Rs 1 crore during the year. In comparison, 13 proposals from Hong Kong, together worth Rs 610.42 crore, received approval, according to official data.These approvals fall under India's investment screening rules for countries sharing a land border with the country. Introduced through Press Note 3 of the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) in April 2020, the policy requires prior government approval for such investments. The regulations were brought in during the Covid-19 pandemic to curb opportunistic takeovers and acquisitions of Indian companies.During April 2025 to March 2026, the government approved 63 FDI proposals with a total investment value of Rs 10,292.67 crore ($1.18 billion), according to DPIIT data.Among all countries whose proposals were cleared, Singapore accounted for the highest approved investment value.Five proposals from the country worth Rs 3,259.88 crore ($382.52 million) received approval.The UK followed with five proposals worth Rs 2,477.67 crore ($283 million), while two proposals from Thailand valued at Rs 1,600 crore (about $180 million) were also cleared.Back in March, the government revised certain provisions of Press Note 3, allowing investors with non-controlling beneficial ownership of up to 10% from land border countries (LBCs) to invest through the automatic route, subject to applicable sectoral caps, entry routes and other conditions.However, the relaxation does not extend to entities registered in China, Hong Kong or any other country sharing a land border with India. The countries sharing land borders with India are China, Bangladesh, Pakistan, Bhutan, Nepal, Myanmar and Afghanistan.Official data also shows that China has remained a relatively small contributor to India's overall FDI inflows. Between April 2000 and March 2026, the country ranked 23rd among FDI sources, accounting for only 0.32% of India's total FDI equity inflows. During the period, Chinese investments totalled $2.51 billion, or Rs 16,162.25 crore.Hong Kong ranked 15th over the same period, with a 0.62% share in total FDI equity inflows into India. Cumulative investments from the territory stood at $4.91 billion, equivalent to Rs 31,220.30 crore.The latest approvals are broadly in line with the previous financial year.In 2024-25, India had also approved only one FDI proposal from China. That proposal was valued at Rs 28.71 crore ($3.44 million).Overall, the government had cleared 82 proposals under the government route during the year, involving investments worth Rs 39,758 crore ($4.72 billion).Hong Kong, meanwhile, received approvals for 11 proposals worth Rs 1,225.28 crore ($146.51 million) during 2024-25.
Article Summary: China's share in India's foreign direct investment (FDI) approvals remained largely negligible in 2025-26. The government approved just one proposal worth Rs 1 crore during the year. In comparison, 13 proposals from Hong Kong, together worth Rs 610.42 crore, received approval.

Article Title: Bullion market: What will guide gold, silver prices this week?
Article Text:
Gold and silver outlook:

Gold and silver prices are expected to move in a narrow range this week as investors await key economic data, especially the US non-farm payrolls report, for clues on the Federal Reserve's next interest rate move.According to analysts, the market will also track purchasing managers' index (PMI) data from the US, the UK, the Eurozone and Japan. July employment data from the US, including non-farm payrolls and the unemployment rate, will be closely watched.Developments related to the US-Iran conflict and the stability of crude oil supplies through key shipping routes will also influence market sentiment.Jateen Trivedi, VP Research Analyst - Commodity and Currency at LKP Securities, told PTI that MCX gold is expected to remain within a limited range in the near term."MCX gold to trade in the Rs 1.40-1.44 lakh per 10 grams range in the near-term, with the directional move hinging on US macroeconomic data and evolving expectations around the Fed's policy path," he said.Gold and silver both ended lower last week. On the Multi Commodity Exchange, August gold futures fell Rs 1,595, or 1.1%, to close at Rs 1.41 lakh per 10 grams. September silver futures dropped Rs 4,940, or 2.2%, to settle at Rs 2.17 lakh per kilogram."Gold remained volatile and ended the week on a weaker note, with MCX Gold declining a little over 1% as prices continued to consolidate within a broad trading range," Trivedi said.He added that gold failed to attract significant buying despite a weaker US dollar and a sharp fall in crude oil prices, showing that investors remained cautious.In the international market, Comex gold futures for October delivery ended marginally lower at $4,076.6 per ounce. Silver futures for September delivery fell nearly 2% over the week to close at $57.78 per ounce in New York.Trivedi said uncertainty over the Federal Reserve's interest rate outlook continued to weigh on bullion prices, as policymakers have not given a clear timeline for future policy moves.Apart from the US jobs data, investors will also watch speeches by Federal Reserve officials Lisa D Cook and Thomas Barkin. China's trade data, including exports, imports, Consumer Price Index and Producer Price Index, will also be in focus for further cues on the global economy and bullion prices.
Article Summary: Gold and silver prices are expected to move in a narrow range this week. Investors await key economic data, especially the US non-farm payrolls report. The market will also track purchasing managers' index (PMI) data from the US, the UK, the Eurozone and Japan.

Article Title: Bankipur bypoll result today: Can Prashant Kishor break BJP's 3-decade hold?
Article Text:
Also Read

(With agency inputs)





PATNA: Counting of votes for the Bankipur assembly bypoll in Bihar began at 8 am on Monday, with the focus on whether Jan Suraaj Party founder Prashant Kishor , making his electoral debut, can wrest the seat from the BJP.The bypoll was necessitated after BJP national president Nitin Nabin resigned from the assembly seat in April following his election to the Rajya Sabha."The counting of votes for the Bankipur by-election began amid tight security arrangements," an official told PTI.The bypoll, conducted on July 30, recorded a voter turnout of 34.30%, marking a decline of over seven percentage points from the 41.45% turnout recorded in the previous assembly election.A total of 26 candidates are contesting the by-election.Nitin Nabin had won the seat for the fifth consecutive time in November 2025, defeating his nearest rival RJD's Rekha Gupta by a margin of more than 50,000 votes. The RJD has once again fielded Gupta for the bypoll.The contest also marks the electoral debut of former poll strategist Prashant Kishor, who founded the Jan Suraaj Party a few years ago.The BJP, which has maintained an unbeaten run in the constituency since 1995 when it was known as Patna West, has fielded youth wing leader Neeraj Kumar Sinha to retain the seat.
Article Summary: Counting of votes for the Bankipur assembly bypoll in Bihar began at 8 am on Monday. The focus is on whether Jan Suraaj Party founder Prashant Kishor can wrest the seat from the BJP. The bypoll was necessitated after BJP national president Nitin Nabin resigned from the assembly seat in April.

Article Title: MHT CET CAP Round 1 allotment 2026 released at cetcell.mahacet.org; candidates must complete seat acceptance by August 5
Article Text:
MHT CET engineering CAP Round 1 results announced; candidates begin admission formalities

MHT CET CAP Round 1

allotment:

How candidates can check allotment status

Seat acceptance options explained

Competition remains high for engineering seats

The State Common Entrance Test Cell, Maharashtra released the provisional CAP Round 1 allotment lists for engineering and management admissions on August 2, 2026. Candidates allotted seats under the Centralised Admission Process (CAP) can now check their allotment status through the respective counselling portals using their Application ID and Date of Birth or password.Candidates who have secured allotments must complete all post-allotment formalities between August 3 and August 5, 2026. The schedule includes seat acceptance, online declaration, payment of the acceptance fee and reporting to the allotted institute within the prescribed deadline. Failure to complete the required steps will affect participation in subsequent counselling rounds wherever applicable.Engineering aspirants can access the provisional allotment by logging into the official FE counselling portal and selecting the "Check Provisional Allotment Status (CAP Round-I)" option. MBA and MMS candidates can view their allotment through the respective counselling portal after entering their login credentials.Candidates must verify the allotted institute and branch before proceeding with the admission process.Candidates allotted their first preference will have their seats automatically frozen. Such candidates must accept the allotment, pay the seat acceptance fee online and report to the allotted institute.They will not be eligible to participate in the remaining regular CAP rounds.Candidates allotted a preference other than their first choice may either self-freeze the allotted seat or choose the Betterment option. Those selecting Betterment must accept the current allotment, pay the seat acceptance fee online and remain eligible for consideration in the next counselling round while retaining the present seat.Candidates are also required to verify the details submitted in their application, including qualifying marks, category, reservation and other claims. Any discrepancy must be reported through the candidate login using the online grievance facility.The first MHT CET attempt recorded 1,32,838 registrations, with 1,16,196 candidates appearing, resulting in an attendance rate of 87.47 per cent. Of those, 1,12,601 candidates belonged to Maharashtra, while 3,595 were from Outside Maharashtra. The examination was conducted at 181 centres across all 36 districts.Institute-wise closing ranks released with the allotment indicate intense competition for Computer Science Engineering, Information Technology, Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning, Data Science, and Electronics and Telecommunication programmes. Top institutions, including COEP Technological University and VJTI, recorded Open category closing ranks between 860 and 960 or lower for leading branches.The counselling process will continue through four regular CAP rounds before institute-level admissions begin.
Article Summary: The State Common Entrance Test Cell, Maharashtra released the provisional CAP Round 1 allotment lists for engineering and management admissions on August 2, 2026. Candidates allotted seats under the Centralised Admission Process (CAP) can now check their allotment status through the respective counselling portals using their Application ID and Date of Birth or password.

Article Title: Capital One says anti-money laundering review led to closure of over 300 Trump Organization accounts
Article Text:
Trump had claimed that blocking was politcally motivated

US President Donald Trump's family business Trump Organization has been accused by Capital One of having its bank accounts closed following an internal anti-money laundering (AML) review, according to a court filing amid ongoing legal battle.In a court filing on Friday, the bank said the account closures were the result of "months of analysis and a careful review" conducted by its AML experts in line with internal policies and regulatory guidance and not politically motivated, as reported by Reuters."Documents and Plaintiffs' own allegations make clear that Capital One closed Plaintiffs' accounts for anti-money laundering ('AML') reasons," the filing said.The accounts were held by the Trump Organization, the privately owned business conglomerate that oversees Trump's hotels, golf courses, real estate and other ventures. Large companies often operate hundreds of bank accounts across different entities and properties. US banks can close customer accounts after internal compliance and risk reviews if they determine the banking relationship no longer meets their anti-money laundering or regulatory standards.Capital One did not directly accuse the Trump Organization of engaging in illegal money laundering. Instead, it argued that the decision was based on compliance and risk assessment procedures, not political considerations.The filing marks the first time a bank has formally stated in court that anti-money laundering concerns were behind its decision to close the Trump Organization's accounts.The bank is seeking dismissal of a lawsuit filed by the Trump Organization and Eric Trump in March 2025 in a Florida federal court. The lawsuit alleges that Capital One closed the accounts because of its "woke" beliefs and to align with the political climate following the January 6, 2021, attack on the US Capitol.Capital One notified the Trump Organization in March 2021 that it would close more than 300 affiliated accounts.The federal court in Miami has already dismissed two versions of the lawsuit while allowing the plaintiffs to amend their complaint. In Friday's filing, Capital One argued that the latest complaint "suffers from the same fundamental flaws" as the previous versions.The bank described the allegations of political bias as "misguided" and said they were "based on cherry-picked quotations unsupported by the full context" of documents submitted to the court."The transaction patterns identified by Capital One are among the types of activity flagged by federal banking guidance," the filing said.The dispute comes as the Trump administration has intensified scrutiny of alleged "debanking" by major financial institutions. Trump signed an executive order in August 2025 barring discriminatory debanking and, earlier this year, filed a separate lawsuit against JPMorgan Chase on similar grounds.The Trump Organization and Eric Trump sued Capital One in March 2025, alleging the bank unlawfully closed more than 300 of their accounts in 2021 because of its "woke" beliefs and to align with the political climate following the January 6, 2021, attack on the US Capitol. They argued the closures amounted to discriminatory "debanking" and sought damages.
Article Summary: Bank says account closures were result of "months of analysis and a careful review" The bank is seeking dismissal of a lawsuit filed by the Trump Organization and Eric Trump. The lawsuit alleges that Capital One closed the accounts because of its "woke" beliefs and to align with the political climate.

Article Title: US crude bound for Israel for first time since 2023
Article Text:
Malta-flagged Aframax tanker Captain John loaded crude at Enbridge's Ingleside terminal near Corpus Christi, Texas and is bound for Israel's southern port of Ashkelon

A cargo of US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude oil is headed to Israel for the first time in nearly three years, according to ship-tracking data.The Malta-flagged Aframax tanker Captain John loaded the crude at Enbridge's Ingleside terminal near Corpus Christi, Texas, on Thursday and is bound for Israel's southern port of Ashkelon, data from LSEG showed, as cited by Reuters.The vessel is carrying around 550,000 barrels of WTI crude, according to LSEG. An Aframax tanker can carry up to 750,000 barrels. The shipment has been chartered by global trading house Vitol, which did not immediately respond to requests for comment.Data from Kpler showed that the last US crude shipment to Israel took place in October 2023.The shipment comes amid the ongoing US-Israel conflict with Iran, which began on February 28 and has significantly disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, a key global energy transit route that previously handled about one-fifth of the world's crude oil and natural gas supplies.
Article Summary: Malta-flagged Aframax tanker Captain John loaded the crude at Enbridge's Ingleside terminal near Corpus Christi, Texas. The vessel is carrying around 550,000 barrels of WTI crude, according to LSEG. The shipment has been chartered by global trading house Vitol.

Article Title: FIFA abandons $4.2-billion World Cup stake sale plan after global backlash
Article Text:
President Donald Trump holds up a red card during a meeting with FIFA president Gianni Infantino

FIFA has abandoned its controversial plan to sell a minority stake in its commercial operations, including the FIFA World Cup, following strong opposition from football federations and internal criticism.FIFA President Gianni Infantino announced on Friday that the proposal would not move forward after it became clear it had created divisions within the global football community."Having listened carefully to all the views, it has become clear that the project has created divisions of a nature that, regardless of the level of support, are no longer in the interest of the objective set out in the first place," Infantino said in a statement, as quoted by Reuters."Our purpose has always been — and will always be — to unite and improve. As a result, this proposal will not proceed," he added.The plan, unveiled earlier this week, proposed raising up to $4.2 billion by selling around a 20% stake in a newly created commercial entity that would manage FIFA events, including the World Cup. FIFA had argued that the investment would generate funds for global football development and rejected claims that it was commercialising the sport.Infantino had also told FIFA's member associations they would receive $40 million each if they approved the proposal by September 19.However, the plan drew swift resistance from football's major continental bodies. UEFA, European football's governing body, accused FIFA of putting the sport's "soul" up for sale and voted unanimously on Thursday to boycott FIFA tournaments unless the proposal was withdrawn.CONCACAF, representing North America, Central America and the Caribbean, also rejected the proposal, while the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) later announced it stood in solidarity with UEFA and CONCACAF. Together, the three confederations represent 143 of FIFA's 211 member associations, making it virtually impossible for the proposal to secure majority approval.The backlash also exposed divisions within FIFA. Senior adviser Carlos Cordeiro resigned with immediate effect, describing the proposal as "a bad deal for football." FIFA Chief Operating Officer Kevin Lamour reportedly told staff they had been "deceived" by Infantino and characterised the initiative as "a project of one person."Seeking to ease tensions, Infantino said he would engage with stakeholders in the coming weeks to find other ways to strengthen the global game, particularly in developing football nations.The abandoned proposal centred on the creation of a $20-billion subsidiary, FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), which would oversee the commercial rights to the World Cup and other FIFA competitions. Thrive Eternal, an investment fund managed by Thrive Capital founder Joshua Kushner, had been expected to lead the investor consortium, which was a main part of the controversy. Joshua is the brother of Jared Kushner, US President Donald Trump's son-in-law. The connection prompted questions over potential political influence, although FIFA maintained the investment process was based on commercial considerations, and Trump said he had not discussed the proposal with Infantino.Infantino, 56, is due to seek re-election as FIFA president next year amid reports that CONCACAF president Victor Montagliani is considering challenging him. British Prime Minister Andy Burnham also criticised Infantino, calling him "the wrong man to lead the organisation."US President Donald Trump, who has developed close ties with Infantino during preparations for the 2026 World Cup co-hosted by the United States, said he had not discussed the investment proposal with the FIFA chief.
Article Summary: FIFA president Gianni Infantino withdraws plan to sell a 20% stake in its commercial operations. The proposal drew strong opposition from football federations and internal criticism. UEFA, European football's governing body, accused FIFA of putting the sport's "soul" up for sale.

Article Title: Tough road for Trump: Why sanctions Bill for tariffs on Russian oil buyers may fail House test
Article Text:
Sanctions and trade experts say it would establish a new precedent by allowing future presidents to use secondary tariffs to target entire countries. (AP photo)

More power for Trump: Why are lawmakers concerned?

What is the US Senate Bill on Russia Sanctions?

Bill to face hurdles?

New precedents on sanctions

US President Donald Trump may not find it easy to get the new bill championing fresh sanctions on Russia and countries that trade with it passed. The proposed legislation would sanction Russian officials and authorise up to 100% tariffs on the five largest importers of Russian crude oil or natural gas, as well as the five countries considered to be the biggest enablers of Moscow's efforts to bypass US sanctions and continue financing its war in Ukraine, now in its fifth year.The Russia sanctions bill pushed for more than a year by the late Senator Lindsey Graham is facing growing resistance in Congress, with Democrats and some Republicans objecting to provisions that would give President Donald Trump sweeping new tariff powers, according to a Reuters report.Lawmakers from both parties, along with industry trade groups, have raised concerns over a section of the legislation that would allow Trump to impose hefty tariffs on countries that buy significant volumes of Russian oil and gas or on nations that his administration determines are helping Russia evade sanctions.While the bill does not identify those countries by name, they would likely include China, India and possibly certain European nations and Japan.Before his sudden death earlier this month, Graham had spent more than a year pushing for the measure. He secured Trump's backing only in recent weeks, as the Republican president became increasingly supportive of Ukraine while growing more frustrated with Moscow, the Reuters report said.The tariff provisions gained added significance for the White House after the US Supreme Court struck down Trump's 10% to 50% "reciprocal" tariffs in February, prompting the administration to look for alternative legal authority to impose such trade measures.Also Read | India faces 100% Trump tariff threat as US Senate advances Russia Sanctions Bill - what it means The legislation also gives the president the authority to waive Russia-related sanctions for unspecified national security reasons. That provision has drawn opposition from pro-Ukraine Democrats, who cite Trump's changing positions on Russia and Ukraine.In addition, the bill would renew for another five years the Iran energy and weapons sanctions first enacted in 1996, which are due to expire this year. That extension was included as a condition for securing Trump's support. Earlier this week, Trump also insisted that tariffs on Iran be added to the legislation, despite the fact that trade between the US and Iran is virtually non-existent.With opinion polls indicating that Democrats could regain control of the House of Representatives and potentially the Senate in the November congressional elections, some lawmakers believe it would be better to delay passage of the Russia sanctions bill until Democrats have greater influence over legislation that many consider unprecedented, the report said.The legislation received overwhelming bipartisan backing in procedural votes in the US Senate on Tuesday and Wednesday, with lawmakers describing it as a tribute to the late Senator Lindsey Graham.Congressional aides said the bill could be approved by the full Senate before lawmakers leave Washington for their home states next week.However, the measure, which has been renamed in Graham's honour, is expected to face a tougher path in the House of Representatives, which is in recess until August 31.Opposition has already emerged from some senior Democrats.Senator Ron Wyden and Representative Richard Neal, the ranking Democrats on the Senate and House trade committees, criticised the legislation, arguing that it would hand Trump broad new tariff powers that could push up inflation in the United States."There is no question that the US ‌government must take ⁠stronger action against purchasers of Russian energy who are fueling the unjustifiable war against Ukraine. But the latest draft of the Sanctioning Russia Act is a prescription for bedlam and higher tariffs," they said in a joint statement.The bill has also sparked concerns among some Republicans.Mahur Patel, a former Republican congressional aide who is now with the Hogan Lovells Cadwalader law firm, said he was sceptical that the legislation would pass the House this year, citing the approaching election season and continued unease among Republicans over the scope of Trump's tariff policies.According to Patel, many Republican lawmakers remain uncomfortable with Trump's earlier sweeping tariffs, with some continuing to press for product-specific exemptions, such as the temporary relief granted this week for phosphate fertiliser imports from Morocco to prevent shortages linked to the Iran war.Apart from concerns that the legislation could add to inflationary pressures in the United States, sanctions and trade experts say it would establish a new precedent by allowing future presidents to use secondary tariffs to target entire countries, rather than limiting action to individuals or entities accused of helping evade sanctions.Although the bill specifies that these powers would expire after five years, experts note that governments rarely relinquish authorities once they have been granted.Supporters of the legislation maintain that the five-year sunset provision sufficiently limits the tariff authority, allowing it to curb Russia's energy revenues without creating broader unintended consequences.Jess Hoversen, a former senior US government official who is now chief economist at developer platform bank Column, said the legislation would, if enacted, hand the government an extremely broad tool capable of affecting entire bilateral trade relationships."Secondary tariffs, as designed in this bill, would function as a much blunter instrument that could apply across-the-board duties to all goods from a country based on its energy trade with Russia or its role in sanctions evasion," Hoversen said.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump may not find it easy to get the new bill championing fresh sanctions on Russia and countries that trade with it passed. The proposed legislation would sanction Russian officials and authorise up to 100% tariffs on the five largest importers of Russian crude oil or natural gas. Lawmakers from both parties, along with industry trade groups, have raised concerns over a section of the legislation.

Article Title: US stock market today: Nasdaq rises as Amazon rallies strongly
Article Text:
Market participants had viewed this week as a crucial test for the technology sector.

US stock market today: Nasdaq outperformed the other major Wall Street indexes on Friday as a 13.7% rally in Amazon shares lifted technology stocks. Amazon joined other Big Tech firms in reporting robust cloud business growth, easing investor concerns over returns from heavy artificial intelligence spending.At 9:47 a.m. ET, the Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 82.26 points, or 0.16%, at 52,290.32. The S&P 500 gained 10.05 points, or 0.12%, to 7,446.54, while the Nasdaq Composite advanced 86.20 points, or 0.34%, to 25,208.37.The S&P 500 consumer discretionary sector led the market, rising 5.2%, driven largely by Amazon's sharp gains, according to a Reuters report.Tech stocks in focusMarket participants had viewed this week as a crucial test for the technology sector. After a strong finish to the second quarter, AI-linked stocks came under pressure in July as investors locked in profits and waited for evidence that substantial AI investments were beginning to translate into meaningful returns despite weaker free cash flow.Amazon on Thursday reported its strongest quarterly revenue growth in more than four years, following similar results from Microsoft and Alphabet earlier this month.The performance encouraged investors to focus on the companies' accelerating growth rather than the sharp decline in free cash flow reported alongside the earnings."Amazon showed us, without a shadow of a doubt, that the web-services or AI side of the business is driving growth for the company," said Adam Sarhan, chief executive of 50 Park Investments in New York according to Reuters."Investors are able to look past the free-cash-flow decline because it is one component. If growth continues, it will make up for that shortfall."However, gains were tempered by Apple, whose shares fell 9.8% in early trade after the company cautioned that supply constraints would weigh on growth. Investors looked beyond the near-term shortages to assess the impact of an anticipated increase in iPhone prices.Microsoft shares rose 1.8% after recording their biggest single-day gain on record in the previous session. Alphabet and Meta each advanced more than 2%, while among semiconductor stocks, Nvidia climbed 1.3% and Micron added 1.6%.Despite the late-week rebound putting all three major Wall Street indexes on course for weekly gains, the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq remained on track to end July in negative territory after AI-related stocks experienced a steep selloff during the month.The week also introduced fresh uncertainty over the interest-rate outlook after the Federal Reserve kept its benchmark rate unchanged. Comments from Chair Kevin Warsh, along with a broadly benign inflation report released on Thursday, prompted traders to raise the probability of rates remaining unchanged in September to 35%, compared with about 18% a week earlier, according to CME's FedWatch tool.
Article Summary: Nasdaq outperformed the other major Wall Street indexes on Friday as a 13.7% rally in Amazon shares lifted technology stocks. Amazon joined other Big Tech firms in reporting robust cloud business growth, easing investor concerns over returns from heavy artificial intelligence spending.

Article Title: Seeking job in US? Trump weighs $100,000 work permit fee from foreign graduates
Article Text:
A proposed $100,000 post-study work fee could make it significantly more expensive for international students to work in the US post graduation

The Trump administration is considering imposing a $100,000 fee on international students seeking to work in the United States after graduating from American universities, according to people familiar with the matter, in a move that could significantly reduce the appeal of studying in the country.The proposed fee would apply to the Optional Practical Training (OPT) programme, which allows international graduates to work in the US on their student visas for up to three years, depending on their field of study. Around 419,000 foreign graduates were working under the OPT programme in 2024, the latest available data show.If approved, the measure would mark another step in President Donald Trump's broader push to tighten legal immigration. It could also deal a blow to US universities, which rely heavily on international students for tuition revenue, and to technology and financial firms that recruit graduates from American universities for skilled roles.The proposal is still under discussion at the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), and it remains unclear whether the White House will approve it. Officials have also not decided whether the fee would be paid by international students themselves or by universities or employers hiring them.A DHS spokesperson said no policy should be considered final until it is formally announced."No policies should be considered final until formally announced. At DHS we are always having conversations about how to use all tools in our arsenal to protect the integrity of our legal immigration system," the spokesperson said.The proposed charge is expected to be linked to a new requirement announced earlier this month requiring international students to apply for an extension of their visas to access OPT. Previously, student visas remained valid through the duration of a student's academic programme and the associated work-authorisation period.The administration is also preparing a broader overhaul of the OPT programme, with revised regulations expected as early as this fall.The proposal follows the administration's earlier attempt to impose a $100,000 fee on H-1B visas for foreign professionals. That fee, announced last year, was blocked by a federal appeals court in Boston last week.While the H-1B levy was eventually narrowed to apply only to foreign professionals seeking to enter the US after facing opposition from major technology companies, a fee on OPT would more directly affect firms that recruit international graduates from American universities before transitioning them to H-1B visas.The $100,000 fee has emerged as a recurring feature of the administration's immigration agenda. Officials are also considering requiring green card applicants outside the US to post a refundable $100,000 bond that would be returned only after they become US citizens.The OPT programme has long been a key incentive for international students choosing to study in the United States. Supporters argue it enables graduates to gain professional experience before returning home or pursuing longer-term employment, while critics contend it allows employers to hire foreign graduates without sufficient safeguards to ensure wages remain comparable to those offered to American workers.During Trump's first term, senior immigration officials, including Stephen Miller, pushed to eliminate the STEM OPT programme, which provides eligible science, technology, engineering and mathematics graduates with up to three years of work authorisation. The proposal was ultimately shelved after opposition from business-oriented members of the administration, including Jared Kushner.
Article Summary: Proposed fee would apply to the Optional Practical Training (OPT) programme. Around 419,000 foreign graduates were working under the OPT programme in 2024. If approved, the measure would mark another step in President Donald Trump's broader push to tighten legal immigration.

Article Title: US economy slows as GDP growth slips to 1.5%, consumers keep momentum alive
Article Text:
Imports emerge as the biggest drag

Inflation eases but stays above target

Resilience amid economic and political pressures

Strong consumer spending and steady business investment helped cushion the US economy in the second quarter, but a surge in imports dragged overall growth to its slowest pace this year, even as inflation showed further signs of easing.Data released by the commerce department on Thursday showed that the world's largest economy grew at an annual rate of 1.5% between April and June, slowing from 2.1% in the first quarter and coming in below economists' expectations.Household spending remained the biggest support for the economy during the quarter. Consumer spending, which accounts for about 70% of US economic activity, accelerated sharply to a 3.2% annual pace from just 0.5% in the January-March period.A broader measure of the economy's underlying strength also pointed to resilience. Excluding the volatile effects of government spending and trade, the economy expanded at a 3.9% annual rate, improving from 1.7% in the previous quarter.Businesses also continued to invest despite slower headline growth. Investment outside the housing sector increased at an annual pace of 8.4%, down from 10.6% in the first quarter but remaining strong, reflecting a surge in artificial intelligence-related investment.The biggest drag on growth came from imports, which climbed at an annual rate of 11.5%. Increased shipments of computer chips and other products supporting AI investment contributed to the rise. Because GDP measures only what is produced within the United States, imports are deducted from the calculation, reducing second-quarter growth by 1.5 percentage points."The consumer rescued the quarter,'' said Olu Sonola, head of US economics at Fitch Ratings. “AI investment remains a powerful growth story, but the import surge underpinning the buildout is a reminder that an AI boom does not automatically translate into an equally large boost to US GDP.”Alongside the GDP figures, the commerce department reported that inflation continued to cool in June, although it remained above the Federal Reserve's target.The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index, the Fed's preferred measure of inflation, rose 3.7% from June 2025, easing from a 4.1% year-on-year increase in May. Core PCE inflation, which excludes food and energy prices, stood at 3.3%, compared with 3.4% in May.On a monthly basis, prices fell 0.1% between May and June, helped by a 9.2% decline in gasoline and other energy prices.Even so, inflation has remained above the central bank's 2% target for more than five years, frustrating policymakers as well as consumers facing a high cost of living ahead of the November midterm elections, now less than 100 days away.The Federal Reserve on Wednesday left its benchmark interest rate unchanged for the fifth consecutive meeting. However, three regional Fed presidents dissented, saying they wanted to raise rates to tackle elevated inflation.The latest figures also highlighted the resilience of the US economy despite the Iran war and the spike in energy prices it triggered. The labour market has strengthened this year after a weak 2025, giving consumers the confidence and income to keep spending.Employers have added an average of 92,000 jobs a month this year, compared with fewer than 10,000 jobs a month in 2025, when high interest rates and President Donald Trump's erratic use of tariffs discouraged businesses from hiring.Political attention remains firmly on the economy ahead of November's midterm elections, which will determine whether President Donald Trump's Republicans retain full control of Congress.A new AP-NORC poll found public opinion has become less favourable towards the Iran war. It also showed that 72% of US adults consider it "extremely" or "very" important to prevent domestic oil and gas prices from rising, up from 67% in March.
Article Summary: US economy grew at an annual rate of 1.5% between April and June, slowing from 2.1% in the first quarter. Consumer spending, which accounts for about 70% of US economic activity, accelerated sharply to a 3.2% annual pace.

Article Title: US stock market today: Wall Street flat; Nasdaq climbs over 1.5% as tech stocks rally
Article Text:
In commodity markets, oil prices eased after recent sharp swings driven by escalating tensions in the Middle East.

US stock market today: Wall Street rebounded on Thursday, led by a sharp rally in Microsoft after the technology giant posted stronger-than-expected quarterly earnings. The S&P 500 rose 0.9%, recovering more than half of Wednesday's decline, its steepest fall in seven weeks. The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 250 points, or 0.5%, while the Nasdaq Composite climbed 1.8%, a day after slipping 9.8% below the record high it reached last month.Microsoft surged 15.2% after reporting quarterly profit that exceeded analysts' expectations, supported by robust growth in its Azure cloud business. Chief Executive Satya Nadella said the performance reflected customers' increasing adoption of Microsoft's AI offerings. Investors also welcomed the company's decision not to significantly raise its AI spending plans, easing concerns that heavy investments in artificial intelligence could strain cash flows without delivering the expected gains in productivity and profitability.In contrast, Meta Platforms dropped 8.9% after reporting quarterly earnings that fell short of forecasts, despite revenue slightly exceeding expectations.Some analysts pointed to the company's decision to raise the lower end of its projected capital spending range for the year as a factor behind the decline.Chipmakers and memory manufacturers recovered some of their recent losses, as investors returned to stocks that had been hit by concerns over stretched valuations following the AI-driven rally. Micron Technology rose 8.4%, reducing its weekly decline to 13%, while Lam Research jumped 18.3% and Advanced Micro Devices advanced 7.3%.Broader markets also drew support from easing Treasury yields after Wednesday's sharp rise. The yield on the benchmark 10-year US Treasury slipped to 4.65% from 4.67%, while the 30-year Treasury yield remained at 5.20% after climbing from 5.09% the previous day.Treasury yields had surged after Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh offered few indications about the central bank's next steps to tackle persistently high inflation. While elevated interest rates help curb inflation, they also weigh on economic growth and reduce the appeal of equities and other risk assets.Economic data released on Thursday showed the US economy expanded more slowly than economists had expected during the spring. Inflation remained above the Federal Reserve's target in the latest month, although it came in slightly below market expectations.In commodity markets, oil prices eased after recent sharp swings driven by escalating tensions in the Middle East. Brent crude, the global benchmark, fell 1.5% to $86.79 a barrel. Prices have fluctuated dramatically this month, falling to as low as $72 before rising to $102 last week amid uncertainty over whether the United States and Iran could reach an agreement allowing oil tankers to move freely from the Middle East to global markets.
Article Summary: The S&P 500 rose 0.9%, recovering more than half of Wednesday's decline. The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 250 points, or 0.5%, while the Nasdaq Composite climbed 1.8%. Microsoft surged 15.2% after reporting quarterly profit that exceeded analysts' expectations.

Article Title: Asian stocks trade mixed after Fed holds rates; Kospi rallies 4%, Shenzhen slips 300 points
Article Text: Asian equities showed signs of stabilising on Thursday, but investors remained cautious after a turbulent week marked by a sharp AI-driven market sell-off, uncertainty over the US interest rate outlook and renewed geopolitical tensions that briefly sent oil prices soaring.Taiwan's benchmark climbed 666.47 points to 40,705.65, up 1.66%, while South Korea's Kospi gained 201.22 points to 5,864.46, rising 3.55%. Japan's Nikkei rose 881.37 points to 62,315.56, up 1.43%.
